patches.decision_note: The evidence index identifies a separately titled product-content page with no suitable page-specific Requirement in the inventory.
NFT image and detail-page rendering fail independently from whether owned NFTs appear in wallet and dashboard views.
Owned-NFT and mint reporting, referral-reward accounting, and prize-pool/platform statistics exhibit separate failure and recovery trajectories.
The generic statement that the page looks quite good does not verify a concrete acceptance behavior of the broad layout Requirement; the message concretely reports only the separate cover failure.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Marcus, please remove the big blocks and redirect that extra $8 to me. The new breakdown should be:
$30 purchase, $12 to me, $10 to the affiliate, and $8 to the block prize pool.

That should improve my bottom line without materially affecting sales, while also making the game mechanics and marketing simpler.

An even arrangement between me and each community member, together with an equal opportunity to win the continuing $900 prizes, feels consistent with the project's ethos.

patches.decision_note: Removing Big Blocks makes the previously required Big Block metadata counter obsolete, so the stale attribute must be deleted.
This referral-code identity failure is already owned by the narrower REQ_NFT_REFERRAL_IDENTITY Requirement and should not be duplicated under broad metadata accuracy.
The implementation claim specifically fixes the NFT's referral identity and is already represented under REQ_NFT_REFERRAL_IDENTITY.
The generic confirmation follows several fixes and does not uniquely verify the broad metadata Requirement.
The failure to open the book is already represented under NFT-holder access and does not specifically establish a reader-navigation failure.
The source establishes only that the commission is absent from the leaderboard, not that the underlying commission allocation failed; the observation belongs to reporting accuracy.
The source establishes only that the ticket is absent from the leaderboard, not that the underlying ticket allocation failed; the observation belongs to reporting accuracy.
The source resolves the issuance rule by stating that every mint, including one without a referral code, produces one randomly assigned ticket; display requirements belong to reporting Requirements.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
The logic itself sounds good to me.

After 34 mints, the leaderboard now shows 24 tickets and 19 commissions, which is perfect.

The NFT attributes are still not right, though. My screenshots show that NFT #42 has 18 tickets and 9 x $35 commissions on the leaderboard, which is correct. When I open NFT #42, the top of the page also correctly displays 18 tickets and 14 referrals. However, its attributes still report only 6 referrals and $85 in total earnings.

patches.decision_note: The client uniquely accepts the immediately preceding proposal that the no-code flow awards six tickets.
